name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+7 district with incumbent Pete Aguilar seeking re-election
Aguilar has raised $4.7M with $3.5M on hand and no outside opposition spending
Republican Stephanie Vargas has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Aguilar is a well-funded incumbent in a Democratic-leaning district, while his opponent has shown no measurable fundraising or outside support, and markets price the race as a near-certain Democratic win. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 20 points stands.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending against Aguilar, or a surge in Vargas fundraising would be the first signs the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about seven points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised $4.7 million and holding $3.5 million on hand, while Republican Stephanie Vargas reports no fundraising. No outside groups are spending against Aguilar.

With no public polls or expert ratings for this race, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap, all pointing to a comfortable Aguilar win. Prediction markets agree, pricing his chances around 95 percent. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate broad.
